From here `heavy_slot.sh` sees a priority waiter's file (`/tmp/gov-os-heavy-prio-1083526`) as dead, tries to remove it, and fails with "Read-only file system". So a sandboxed caller does not defer to priority waiters as DEC-1011 intends. (2) `/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-123` is read-only in this sandbox, so I used `gov launch`'s TMPDIR as the brief allows. (3) Each `gov retrieve` run makes outbound attempts to `ollama.com:443`, which the sandbox denies.
risks: (a) The planted daemon's `/proc/<pid>/exe` is Python, not the planted script. An implementation that identifies its server by `exe` rather than by the command line (S4 says command line) would fail the hung-restart test. The README says so. (b) `new_pid` is read as the started server's own pid. A wrapper that does not `exec` (for example a shell left in between) would give another pid. (c) The timing assertions use probe_slow 1.5 s and probe_hung 4 s, with the slow stand-in answering at 2.5 s, and determinism expects at least two requests in flight with 0.2 s per request. They have margin but depend on a machine that is not saturated.
lessons: A shebang script's command line is `[interpreter, script, serve]`, so to plant `<executable> serve` exactly, use a bash wrapper that runs `exec -a "$0" <python> serve` from the folder holding a file named `serve`. Inside it `sys.executable` becomes the planted path, so anything it starts must name the real Python explicitly. `ThreadingHTTPServer` needs `block_on_close = False`, or a stand-in that never answers blocks teardown.
